fluff.overview: The Blood Reaper is a seventy-ton Clan BattleMech introduced in 3079 by Clan Wolf's W-7 Facilities on Weingarten. Commissioned by Khan Vlad Ward as a symbolic rallying point for Wolf warriors, the design was intended to standardize the Clan's touman by replacing non-Wolf designs acquired during the Jihad era. Drawing inspiration from several highly successful Clan Wolf machines, particularly the Tundra Wolf and Timber Wolf, the Blood Reaper is a straightforward second-line design emphasizing survivability, firepower, and proven technology. The design proved immediately popular among Wolf warriors and quickly became one of the touman's iconic machines alongside the Mad Cat and Tundra Wolf.
fluff.capabilities:
Built on a Type W4 Endo Steel frame with a 280-rated XL fusion engine, the Blood Reaper achieves a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, deliberately slower than most front-line OmniMechs but compensated by four BMP Series XV jump jets providing a hundred-twenty-meter jump capability. This mobility profile reflects the design's intended role as a tenacious second-line combatant rather than a swift striker.

The Blood Reaper's armament centers on a pair of CC 6-Rack Advanced Tactical Missile Launchers mounted in the side torsos, providing exceptional multi-range flexibility. Three tons of ammunition per launcher allow MechWarriors to carry mixed loads of standard, extended-range, and high-explosive ATM munitions, adapting engagement tactics on the fly. Twin Type 22 Extended Range PPCs in each arm deliver devastating long-range striking power, while a pair of General Systems Heavy Medium Lasers offer enhanced close-range punch. Eighteen double heat sinks manage the substantial thermal demands of this weapons array, though sustained alpha strikes require careful heat discipline.

Advanced/3 armor provides solid protection for the chassis weight, and the design's rugged construction reduces the likelihood of critical component failures under sustained fire, reflecting the engineers' emphasis on battlefield durability over cutting-edge sophistication.
fluff.history:
The Blood Reaper emerged from the political dynamics of post-Jihad Clan Wolf under Khan Vlad Ward's leadership. Determined to purge non-Wolf designs from the touman and forge a unified martial identity, Ward challenged his scientist caste to create a symbolic weapon worthy of the Clan's heritage. The resulting design drew heavily from the Mad Cat's proven chassis and structural layout while incorporating complementary elements from the Black Hawk, producing a machine that honored Wolf tradition in a way the Tundra Wolf (another successful second-line design) had not.

Production commenced at W-7 Facilities on Weingarten in 3079, with the factory complex (a series of mobile industrial facilities originally established during the Jihad) ramping up output rapidly. Ward overcame the typical Clan stigma against second-line machines through characteristic posturing, insisting that warriors truly worthy of the Wolf spirit would prove themselves victorious regardless of their mount. This challenge resonated throughout the touman, and the Blood Reaper was quickly embraced alongside the Mad Cat and Tundra Wolf as one of the Wolves' iconic machines.

The design saw its trial by fire in 3079 when the first Star of Blood Reapers engaged a Trinary of Clan Hell's Horses who attempted a flanking maneuver through what they believed were untested prototypes. The Horses failed to recognize the trap and suffered devastating losses, with only two light and medium 'Mechs escaping the engagement. This decisive victory validated the design and cemented its reputation within the Wolf touman.

Alpha Galaxy warriors received priority allocation, with most Blood Reapers initially assigned to Bloodnamed warriors. Ward leveraged the design politically as well, offering Blood Reapers as replacements to any Galaxy Commander whose units fielded machines deemed unworthy of the Wolf, accelerating the standardization of the touman. At a Wolf Grand Council meeting two weeks after the initial combat trial, Ward outlined his vision of forging a touman worthy of Kerensky's chosen, and the Blood Reaper became central to that effort.

The Blood Reaper 2 variant followed within a year, finding particular favor in Trials of Position and dueling circles. When Clan Wolf relocated to establish the Wolf Empire, production of the original variants at Weingarten continued through the Dark Age before the facility eventually passed to Clan Hell's Horses. The design's legacy continued through W-12 Facilities on Zosma, where the modernized Blood Reaper 3 entered production during the ilClan era, incorporating advanced targeting systems and updated weaponry to ensure the chassis remained competitive against increasingly sophisticated opponents.
fluff.deployment: Released within a year of the original in 3080, the Blood Reaper 2 sacrifices the four jump jets in favor of two arm-mounted Medium Pulse Lasers. This trade exchanges tactical mobility for significantly enhanced close-range firepower, making the variant particularly dangerous in confined terrain and urban environments. The addition of accurate pulse-based weapons complements the existing heavy medium lasers, creating a devastating short-range battery that proved especially popular for Trials of Position, where its concentrated firepower and heavier heat burden (demanding careful management to avoid overheating) became a favored test of a warrior's skill and discipline. Production volume reportedly matched or exceeded the standard variant.
